hints: Focus on what gas density tells you, mass of 1 dm3 can be scaled up to mass of 1 mole using the room temperature molar volume.
One mole of any gas occupies 24 dm3 under room conditions, so multiply 2.42 by 24 to get the approximate $M_r$ near 58.
Decode each skeletal line structure to its molecular formula and check which one gives $M_r$ of 58 for a $C_4H_{10}$ hydrocarbon.
walkthrough:
**Convert density to $M_r$**

Density is mass per volume. For a gas we can scale this to molar mass.

Molar volume under room conditions:
$$1 \text{ mol gas} = 24 \text{ dm}^3$$

So:
$$M_r = \text{density} \times 24 = 2.42 \times 24 \approx 58.1$$

**Decode the skeletal formulae**

Remember each end and bend is a carbon, with enough hydrogens to make 4 bonds.

Structure 1 is a 4-carbon chain with only single bonds: butane, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_{10}$.
$$M_r = (4 \times 12) + (10 \times 1) = 58$$

Structure 2 is a triangle with a methyl branch: methylcyclopropane, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8$.
$$M_r = (4 \times 12) + (8 \times 1) = 56$$

Structure 3 contains a double bond: but-2-ene, $\text{C}_4\text{H}_8$.
$$M_r = (4 \times 12) + (8 \times 1) = 56$$

**Match to the measured density**

Only structure 1 has $M_r = 58$, matching the value from density.

Structures 2 and 3 both have $M_r = 56$, so their density would be slightly lower, about $2.33 \text{ g dm}^{-3}$. Therefore only 1 is possible.

options.A: Incorrect. This would mean 1, 2 and 3 are all possible. While 1 matches $M_r$ 58, 2 and 3 are both $C_4H_8$ with $M_r$ 56, so they do not fit the density.
options.B: Incorrect. This would include 2 as well as 1. Structure 2 is methylcyclopropane, $C_4H_8$, $M_r$ 56, not 58. Students choosing this often miscount the ring carbons or forget rings reduce H count by 2.
options.C: Incorrect. This would mean 2 and 3 only. Both are alkenes or cycloalkanes with general formula $C_nH_{2n}$, giving $M_r$ 56 here. They are too light for a density of 2.42 g dm-3.
options.D: Correct. This is 1 only. Structure 1 is butane, $C_4H_{10}$, with $M_r$ = 58, which exactly matches $2.42 \times 24$. It is also a gas under room conditions, as expected.
